slides.say: Roni has sixty thousand shekels. He invests half of the money in a savings plan that gives a profit of eight percent a year. He invests the rest of the money in a fund that gives a profit of between four percent and sixteen percent a year. Roni's profit in the coming year will be at least what part of the total amount he invested, and at most what part?

slides: We can solve this without calculating the profit in shekels. Remember, eight percent means eight for every hundred invested. Here, only half the total money earns that rate.

slides.say: Before the idea behind the question, let's take a simpler example. Say I have a hundred shekels, and a plan that gives ten percent. If I invest all hundred shekels, I earn ten shekels, which is ten percent of my money.
at: Say I have a hundred shekels

slides.say: But if I invest only half, fifty shekels, I earn ten percent of fifty, which is five shekels. And out of my hundred shekels, five shekels is five percent.
at: But if I invest only half
I earn ten percent of fifty

slides: The plan still pays ten percent on the money I put in. But I invested only half of all my money, so the profit is five percent of the whole amount. That's the whole idea.

slides.say: Back to Roni. Half of his money is in the plan with eight percent. If all of his money were there, he'd earn eight percent. But it's only half the money, so out of the total, he earns half of eight, four percent.
at: so out of the total, he earns half of eight

slides.say: The other half is in the fund, with four to sixteen percent. Again, it's only half the money, so out of the total, he earns half of that. Half of four is two, and half of sixteen is eight. So between two and eight percent.

Now we add the two profits, both measured as percentages of all his money. Careful: don't add the plans' full rates, eight plus four or eight plus sixteen. That would give twelve and twenty-four, choice number one. Each rate applies to only half his money. So we add their contributions to the whole, after halving each rate.

The plan always contributes four percent of the total money, so only the fund changes. At the least, four plus two, six percent. At the most, four plus eight, twelve percent. So between six and twelve percent. Choice number three is our answer. We solved it just by understanding, without calculating the profit in shekels.
at: At the least, four plus two
At the most, four plus eight
Choice number three is our answer

slides.say: By the way, if you still choose to calculate, there are shortcuts here too. Say you worked out eight percent of thirty thousand, the half in the plan. One percent of thirty thousand is three hundred, so eight percent is two thousand four hundred.

You don't need to start over for four percent and sixteen percent. Four is half of eight, so it's half of two thousand four hundred, one thousand two hundred. And sixteen is twice eight, so it's four thousand eight hundred.

And one more shortcut. Say you found the minimum first, six percent. Stop and look at the choices. Only one choice starts with six percent, choice number three, so you don't need the maximum at all. Remember, the answers help us. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: Only one choice starts with six
